To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the charginos and neutralinos of a supersymmetric left- right model can be produced at the CDF with cross sections that are of the same order of magnitude as the cross sections of other SUSY models; and (2) in this model, charginos and neutri- nos can be produced at CDF with cross-sections large enough to be observable, if their mass is not too high (M less than or equal to 100 GeV).
the chargino-neutralino pair production cross section is measured at the CDF experiment for the first time.
we have found a new class of supersymmetric left-right models that can be probed by CDF in the near future.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of supersymmetry at the Tevattron collider.
the study of the production and decay of charginos and neutralinos in the supersymmetric left-right extension of the standard model.
the production of chargino pairs and the production of neutralino pairs in left-right symmetric models of weak interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no significant signals of the production of supersymmetric chargino and/or neutralino pairs at CDF, in agreement with the results of the previous searches.
the CDF data are in agreement with the SM, with a slight excess in some regions of pt and dilepton mass.
no significant evidence of the existence of the charginos and neutralinos has been found.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have studied the production of chargino-neutralino pairs in a left-right symmetric model.
the chargino and the neutralino masses are constrained by our results to be less than 100 GeV and 80 GeV respectively.
the CDF data are consistent with the supersymmetric left-right theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a supersymmetric model with a large left-right mixing, a significant number of charginos and neutralinos can be produced with pt > 20 GeV.

the CDF data on the cross section of pp to chi 10 chi 20+X, in the range 0<pt<40 GeV, is consistent with the cross section of the process pp to chi 0(1) chi (+/-)0(+/-)X, where chi 0(2) and chi 0(4) are assumed to be stable.

, for a large region of the parameter space, the signal of the process pp to chi 10+ chi 20+X is not observable, but the process pp to ch1+ ch 1- is observable, and the signal is expected to be visible in the region pt>40-60 GeV.
